images.title: A square and its sides
images.purpose: Show a square with all four sides marked 7 cm, so that one number is enough: the area is the side times itself and the perimeter is 4 times the side.
images.composition: The square on the left with its four equal sides labelled, three lines of working on the right.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. At the top, centred at x 728 and y 62, the heading A square in dark #1F2937 bold sans-serif (44 px). Left, one square 350 by 350 px at x 150 to 500 and y 150 to 500, filled teal #0072B2 with a thick dark #2B2B2B outline (6 px) and no inner lines. The four sides carry the same label: above the top side, centred at x 325 and y 120, 7 cm; below the bottom side, centred at x 325 and y 536, 7 cm; left of the left side, centred at x 90 and y 325, 7 cm; right of the right side, centred at x 570 and y 325, 7 cm; all four in dark #1F2937 bold (36 px). To the right, at x 800, three lines of text: Area = 7 × 7 = 49 square cm at y 270, Perimeter = 4 × 7 = 28 cm at y 350 and the line All sides equal at y 190 (40 px, dark #1F2937). In all 1 square, 4 side labels and 3 lines of text. No other number and no other text anywhere. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
a figure that is not a square, or sides with different labels
any value other than the listed labels
images.takeaway: A square has equal sides, so its area is length times length and its perimeter is 4 times the length.
images.description: A square with every side 7 cm: area 7 × 7 = 49 square cm and perimeter 4 × 7 = 28 cm.
images.context: Concept image for Squares: Length × Length and 4 × Length. It follows the idea of the square in your maths book (all sides equal) and uses the numbers of this concept's own example.
images.teaching_notes: Let the student say the four sides are all 7 cm before reading the two lines of working. The slip to watch: mixing up 7 × 7 and 4 × 7.

image_decisions.why: The square with four equal labels shows why one number is enough.
